entry.title: Escaping SPACE: Part II (28 minute read)
entry.content:

entry.title: MCP vs CLI vs Skills: What Each Costs in Context (11 minute read)
entry.content:
MCP servers significantly increase token use, adding thousands of input tokens per request, unlike CLI or skill methods. On Sonnet 5.5, a simple task showed MCP consuming 59,417 tokens with default tools against CLI's 1,421 and skill's 3,315, highlighting the high cost of tool-heavy MCP setups. Implementing Tool Search can cut token costs by deferring tool definitions, reducing upfront toolset costs to under 600 tokens for optimal efficiency.

entry.title: LLMs can learn some multi-step reasoning on filler tokens instead of visible CoT (9 minute read)
entry.content:
By changing the training setup and applying LoRAs to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and gpt-oss-20b, researchers taught models to do some multi-step tasks while emitting only filler tokens, beating an answer-only baseline on three of seven tasks. They also mapped theoretical layer-depth limits and showed empirical walls, with some tasks learned out to 60 steps and others failing after one to three. The work is meant to separate filler-token reasoning from steganographic hidden reasoning when interpreting chain-of-thought.

entry.title: Q3.5 Timelines Update: Looks Like the Intelligence Explosion Will Happen in 2027 After All (125 minute read)
entry.content:

AIs that can automate all white-collar work are predicted to arrive before 2028. Companies are currently not on track to align an SAR, and using a misaligned SAR to do recursive self-improvement will have negative consequences. China will probably be able to steal the training recipe and maybe even the model weights if an SAR is trained in the near future.

entry.title: What objective is reasoning solving? (12 minute read)
entry.content:
Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.

From TLDR AI · 2026-11-10 · Engineering & Research

entry.title: Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling (28 minute read)
entry.content:
Test-time scaling trades compute for performance at test time. There are two types of test-time scaling: one allows researchers to trade more compute for more performance per task, but only up to the maximum quantity of per-task compute used during training; and the other lets researchers trade more compute for more performance per task, and lets them do so up to quantities of compute and performance that never occurred during training. Scaling methods that permit the latter change will have a larger impact than test-time scaling considered simply. This essay describes how this may impact the world.
